subject: Applicable mandate at decision time
statement: The decision-time question is not which mandates a program can serve but which governed mandate applies to this Decision Subject / Inventory Block at this effective time, and why.

subject: Scope-hypothesis falsification method
statement: Principal test: a scope hypothesis predicts each entity at that scope carries exactly one mandate; one counterexample falsifies.
verbatim: A scope hypothesis predicts that each entity at that scope carries exactly one mandate. One counterexample falsifies.
speaker: Principal
notes: Evidence set is the §30 mapping — document flags this circularity (2940).

subject: Capital Pool / Inventory Block as mandate carriers (H3/H4)
statement: Principal verdicts: Capital Pool scope NOT FALSIFIED BUT VACUOUS (arbitrary re-pooling absorbs observations; one pool per decision = decision scope under another name); Inventory Block scope NOT FALSIFIED BY CONSTRUCTION/CIRCULAR (block identity incorporating role/mandate makes the claim true by definition).

subject: Decision Aspect hypothesis
statement: Principal's surviving hypothesis: Mandate binds at decision-aspect scope (strike selection, premium acceptance, sizing, exit targeting), each aspect under exactly one frame; Program×Mandate n-to-n is a projection of too coarse a key; aggregate mandate sets are descriptive, never prescriptive; Policy Rules declare which frame governs which aspect.
verbatim: Mandate binds at decision-aspect scope: each governed decision aspect (strike selection, premium acceptance, sizing, exit targeting, etc.) is evaluated under exactly one frame, while a compound decision can contain multiple single-frame aspects.
speaker: Principal

notes: This distinction became the surviving line: §32 'durable declared purpose' and Model B (61:4149-4160).

subject: Mandate shopping defense
